productDirection.summary: Canvas Fogworks is both a general visual/pixel editor and a game-authoring environment.

items.summary: Record a Windows Sandbox pass of the extended installer lifecycle (legacy 0.0.4 project migration, assisted GUI per-user and per-machine install/uninstall, silent per-machine install/uninstall) and a separate host hardware-GPU validation. The guest now writes result.json through the staged Node writer and sets status passed only when that file already meets the guest half of check:installer-evidence, including smoke logs; assisted clicks try UI Automation invoke or selection first; per-machine phases fail closed unless the guest is elevated. No extended Sandbox result.json or host hardware-gpu.json has been recorded. Exit 2 with no files remains the open manual gate rather than a pass. The September 7 per-user software-rendered synthetic-upgrade pass did not cover those phases. Virtual GPU stays disabled. Personal publisher metadata and signing remain intentionally omitted.

Continue extracting cohesive panels and workflows from App.tsx. The layers panel, document toolbar (theme, state, timeline, light, background, screen), project files, image-sequence import, workspace/runtime controls, the 3D inspector, the folders drawer, the script and token panels, and the timeline transport are tested seams. Inspector remnants (states, slots, variants, metadata) and import placement callbacks remain in App.tsx.

Extend delivered schema-88 gameplay (graphs through callable functions, lifecycle and custom events, typed entity and current-level variables, named inputs, 2D/3D interaction/spawning/checkpoints and current-level progress). Player-progress v6 now keeps visited-level snapshots and game-scoped values across transitions; v1–v5 saves still load. The editor and both players now rebind those named inputs from a Controls panel and store version-1 bindings outside the document; malformed settings fall back to the defaults. A package or caller can name up to eight previous content hashes and the progress versions those saves may use; only that explicit list is rewritten onto the current build, and loading it does not by itself write the new slot. Forced kills of the progress writer at partial-write, flush, pre-rename, post-rename and directory-fsync leave a fresh process able to read the last committed slot. That is not a power-loss proof or a GUI renderer crash. Full prefabs remain open, and there is no editor control for authoring the migration list.

Delivered clean-profile standalone 3D acceptance, custom font packaging, unsupported-feature diagnostics, unsigned release provenance, embedded sound playback and screen-space 2D text in the packaged 3D view. Buffer, image and HDR payloads can be streamed beside the manifest and read when a level asks for them; glTF/GLB JSON and fonts stay inline, and the 32 MiB payload budget is unchanged. The acceptance smoke removes the source and font directories, then checks WebGL presentation, packaged font registration, drawn overlay text, a played embedded cue and a path-free provenance record. check:player-exe-evidence scores a clean-machine unpacked EXE record covering WebGL, Stop, the packaged font, overlay text, the embedded cue, path-free provenance, a level transition and a streamed payload. No such record is in the repo, and exit 2 with no file is the open manual gate rather than a pass. Signatures, publisher identity, world-partition streaming and the complete F1 gate remain open.

Extend delivered OBB/sphere contacts and opt-in gravity/restitution with dynamic-body impulses, angular dynamics, slopes/character behavior, hierarchical collider transforms and a replaceable backend boundary.
Extend delivered embedded sound cues and bounded Web Audio playback with a total decoded-byte cache budget, streaming music, buses and dedicated reusable audio assets.

Delivered browser recovery restore, desktop crash/relaunch automation, transactional dependency-folder rollback, and measured durability checkpoints on top of bounded linked-level/image/3D relocation. Atomic replacement fsyncs the parent directory when the platform allows it, and the next replacement or cross-folder Save As deletes a stale atomic-write temporary file left by an unclean shutdown. Dependency payload bytes are fsynced, then the copy journal is replaced with a filesSynced record and that record's bytes are flushed, before the journal name is removed. The next cross-folder Save As still deletes only files and directories an in-progress journal created. A journal that still says filesSynced keeps those copies and removes only itself. filesSynced means those file sync calls returned. Recovery does not replace Save and does not apply over a newer explicit save. Power-loss durability is still not claimed: a crash before a directory fsync returns can still show the in-progress journal or drop a new name, a disk that ignores flush can still lose bytes that sync reported, and a platform that refuses directory fsync can still drop a new name. Renamed self-linked entry files and external image URLs stay refused; project relocation does not copy custom fonts.

Informational release budgets stay frozen from the September Windows Iris Xe sample and the 2026-09-28 Linux Xeon run, using CPU/GPU, 1024 raster, 500-instance, 100-mesh and disk-reload benchmarks plus a mixed soak, noisy 2048 rasters, larger textured scenes and exact history JSON accounting. Additional host samples are stored beside those budgets and do not move them. The original Linux host has no hardware WebGL; llvmpipe stays a separate software record and is not a hardware budget. A later 2026-09-28 cloud Xeon VM recorded another CPU sample, an unavailable WebGL context, and a labeled llvmpipe sample from unsafe SwiftShader; those three files do not move the frozen budgets. No hardware-independent CI gate is enabled. Further physical GPU hosts are still required before that gate. These samples do not justify a renderer rewrite.
Decide whether SVG and Canvas need WebGL-equivalent per-fragment mesh-relief normals and self-occlusion; flat-surface scene lighting is now shared.
Implement minmax/fit-content tracks and remaining explicit grid-placement refinements.
Restore incremental dirty-state reuse for documents containing component instances.
Defer AI, full plugins and collaboration until production-hardening work is established.
